stem: A clinician is documenting a gonadal examination in a child and notes that one testis is not in the scrotum and lies outside the normal line of descent to the scrotum. What is the most accurate term?

options.text: Arrested along the normal line of descent

explanation: Ectopic testis is the correct term. A testis that lies outside the normal pathway of descent is described as ectopic rather than simply undescended along the usual line.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because this describes a testis that is undescended but still located along the normal line of descent.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because a retractile testis can be brought into the scrotum and remain there temporarily.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because a testis located outside the normal line of descent is ectopic.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because intravaginal torsion is a twisting injury, not a term for testicular position.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because buried penis is a penile appearance issue, not a description of testicular location.
